record_type_quote: In the present study, we obtained a new (non-overlapping with the NRCBM dataset) of EHRs data from THIN, containing cases and matched controls for depression diagnosis among males and females aged between 15 and 24.

targets.authors: Nichols L, Ryan R, Connor C, Birchwood M, Marshall T
targets.title: Derivation of a prediction model for a diagnosis of depression in young adults: a matched case–control study using electronic primary care records
targets.evidence_quote: Our target study is that of Nichols et al. [ 48 ] [henceforth, NRCBM] who reported results of models trained on EHRs to predict depression among four groups of young people: females aged 15–18 (F 15–18), females aged 19–24 (F 19–24), males aged 15–18 (M 15–18), and males aged 19–24 (M 19–24).
targets.outcome_quote: In summary, our results demonstrate that the work of Nichols et al. is largely reproducible and replicable. This was the case both for the replication of the original model and the out-of-sample replication applying NRCBM coefficients to our new EHRs data.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The explicit overall verdict is largely replicable. Predictor selection disparities are discussed but do not supersede this overall verdict. All analyses use new non-overlapping records, so reproducing the methodology and alternative models are replication and extension rather than reproduction of original data.

reasoning: Title, DOI and authors match. One target paper; four demographic subsets are not four originals. Original data were unavailable, so the authors’ use of reproducibility describes methods on new data.
